status: Round 1 of 3 scored (7:10 AM ET; h3dec_flow and the DWD head fine-tune pending: their GPUs were taken back). Round 2 (hybrids, GAN, video latents, tiled latents) waits for GPUs (~9:30 AM ET)
verdict: Partly. A sampling decoder that refines H3's own decode gets a small, significant gain from the same latent (+0.56 dB, DISTS -0.004), and a regression decoder gets +1.7 dB on single images, but by eye nothing beats H3's decoder yet, and H3's decoder in video mode is stronger than every child.
numbers: H3's decoder, single-image path: PSNR 30.42 dB, DISTS 0.070, LPIPS-vgg 0.159, 714 ms per 512² image (on tiled latents: 30.42 / 0.066)

refiner (PMRF: H3's decode + noise, a 4-step flow conditioned on the latent): ONE sample 30.97 dB, DISTS 0.066 (95% CI of the change excludes 0), sharper; by eye 4 wins, 8 losses, 60 ties: indistinguishable. Without the latent: 30.82 dB, DISTS 0.068 (not significant): the latent adds +0.15 dB beyond H3's decode
pixreg (68 M regression decoder, 70 min on 1 A100): 32.14 dB, DISTS 0.051, 51 ms, but blind judges preferred H3's decoder 28 to 4: it is blurrier
DWD (Decoding Without a Decoder) replicates on H3: a linear head on the DiT's last-layer tokens decodes 26.06 dB vs 24.43 dB from the latent itself (still far below a real decoder)
H3's decoder in VIDEO mode (whole-clip latent) gets 33.3 dB on the same frames: round 2 tests decoders on video latents
Reference points: §25 optimized latent through H3's decoder 35.22 dB (12 images); FLUX.2 VAE round trip 38.89 dB
